newsitem.title: UK: UK govt promises full debate and referendum on EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK govt promises full debate and referendum on EMU.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government pledged on Wednesday to hold a "real national debate" on the pros and cons of joining a single European currency and to hold a referendum before any decision was made.
The government also promised to play a constructive role in negotiations over EMU whether it joined or not, while always guarding Britain's best interests.
"(My government) will play a full part in the debate about Economic and Monetary Union," a speech written for Queen Elizabeth by cabinet ministers said.
The Queen delivered the speech to formally open the new session of parliament following the May 1 election.

A government note accompanying the speech said there were "formidable obstacles" in the way of Britain joining the first wave of European economic and monetary union, if it starts on January 1, 1999 as planned.

"Nothing will be ruled in or out until the arrangments have been considered in full detail," the note said. But for Britain to join EMU in the forthcoming parliament, the cabinet would have to agree, as would parliament, and a national referendum would have to return a "Yes" vote, it said.
"The government is committed to playing a full part in the debate to influence it in Britain's interests," the note said.
It said key decisions on EMU would be taken during Britain's presidency of the council in the first half of 1998.
